get.description:
This endpoint allows the users to retrieve a list of users within the account. This endpoint supports filtering, pagination, and sorting, as well as including additional information with the response.
It is important to note that after using the pageSize parameter, the "totalSize" in the response represents the total number of available users, not the number of users resulting from the query string.

ManagedBy.description:
Indicates which system manages this user account.   This determines whether the user is managed externally or directly within the Eagle Eye Networks Video Management System (VMS).
This value affects what operations are allowed through the API for this user.   Specifically, the `effectivePermissions` and `schema` objects should be used to determine what actions are permitted in the current session.
Possible values:
  * `scim`  – The user is managed by an external identity provider using SCIM.
  * `bss`   – The user is managed by Brivo Security Suite.

sort.name: sort
sort.description:
Comma separated list of of fields that should be sorted. By default, the users response is sorted by first name.
 * `sort=` - not providing any value will result in error 400
 * `sort=+firstName,+firstName` - same values will result in error 400
 * `sort=-firstName,+firstName` - mutually exclusive values will return error 400
 * There is no limit on the number of sort fields. All available sort fields can be combined freely, as the backend supports sorting by all of them.
 * qRelevance is optional ordering parameter which is available if q filter is used, if q filter is not passed qRelevance as ordering parameter will return error 400

firstName__in.name: firstName__in
firstName__in.description: Filter to get the users whose firstName is on the provided list. The lookup is exact but case insensitive

firstName__contains.name: firstName__contains
firstName__contains.description: Filter to get the users whose the firstName contains the provided substring. The lookup is exact but case insensitive

lastName__in.name: lastName__in
lastName__in.description: Filter to get the users whose lastName is on the provided list. The lookup is exact but case insensitive

lastName__contains.name: lastName__contains
lastName__contains.description: Filter to get the users whose the lastName contains the provided substring. The lookup is exact but case insensitive

email__contains.name: email__contains
email__contains.description: Filter to get the users whose the email contains provided substring. The lookup is exact but case insensitive

permissions.administrator.name: permissions.administrator
permissions.administrator.description: Filter to get the users with provided administrator value.

status.loginStatus__in.name: status.loginStatus__in
status.loginStatus__in.description: Filter to get the users whose loginStatus is on the provided list. The lookup is exact but case insensitive

q.name: q
q.description: Text search that is applied to multiple fields. The fields being searched are defined by the backend and can be changed without warning. Example fields being searched: `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`.

qRelevance__gte.name: qRelevance__gte
qRelevance__gte.description: Sets the current minimum similarity threshold that is used with the `q` parameter. The threshold must be between 0 and 1 (float, default is 0.5).

id__in.name: id__in
id__in.description: Filter to get the users whose id is on the provided list. The lookup is exact and case insensitive.

id__notIn.name: id__notIn
id__notIn.description: Filter to exlude the users whose ids are in the provided list. The lookup is exact and case insensitive.

pageToken.name: pageToken
pageToken.description:
Token string value that references a page for pagination. This value is received when retrieving the first page in the `nextPageToken` and `prevPageToken` fields.
When a pageToken is provided, the backend remembers search parameters from the original request, so search  parameters that affect the result set or order are optional and will be ignored if provided. Representation  parameters like `include` should still be applied.

pageSize.name: pageSize
pageSize.description: The number of entries to return per page. The maximum range of valid page sizes is documented with minimum and  maximum values, but the range might be further limited dynamically based on the requested information, account, and system status. Values outside of the (dynamic) allowed range will not result in an error, but will be clamped to the nearest limit. Thus, logic to detect the last page should not be based on comparing the requested size with the received size, but on the existence of a `nextPageToken` value.

ManagedBy.description:
Indicates which system manages this user account.   This determines whether the user is managed externally or directly within the Eagle Eye Networks Video Management System (VMS).
This value affects what operations are allowed through the API for this user.   Specifically, the `effectivePermissions` and `schema` objects should be used to determine what actions are permitted in the current session.
Possible values:
  * `scim`  – The user is managed by an external identity provider using SCIM.

allOf.description:
Default permission settings to be applied when a reseller creates a new end-user account.
**Visibility and Access:** - Only returned to and editable by the reseller account itself - Not visible to end-user accounts
**When these defaults are applied:** - When a reseller creates a new end-user account through the API - These default values become the initial permission settings for the new account - After account creation, permissions can be modified individually through
  the account's permissions field

**Scope:** - These defaults only affect end-user accounts created under this reseller account - They do not retroactively apply to existing accounts
All properties are inherited from the Permissions schema and have the same behavior and restrictions. See the Permissions schema for detailed descriptions of each permission field.

enabled.description: Indicates that the roles based access control can be enabled for users.

Permissions1.description:
Permission settings that control access to various operational features. These settings apply to all users in end-user accounts, except reseller administrators who switch into the account.
**Visibility and Access:** - Only returned to and editable by the reseller - Not visible or editable by users within the end-user account itself
These settings only apply to end-user accounts. They are not returned for reseller accounts, and attempting to set them on reseller accounts will result in an error.
The permissions are hierarchical - each level includes all restrictions from the previous level. For example, setting editBillableSettings to false includes all restrictions from addDeleteDevices: false, plus additional restrictions.

addDeleteDevices.description:
Controls whether users can add or delete devices such as bridges, cameras, speakers, etc.
When false: • Cannot add new devices to the account • Cannot delete existing devices from the account

editBillableSettings.description:
Controls whether users can change settings that affect subscription costs.
When false, includes all restrictions from addDeleteDevices: false, plus additional restrictions such as: • Cannot change cloud retention periods • Cannot change video resolution settings • Cannot upgrade account editions • Cannot configure analytics that affect billing

editAdvancedSettings.description:
Controls whether users can change settings that could impact cost, performance, stability, or quality.
When false, includes all restrictions from editBillableSettings: false, plus additional restrictions such as: • Cannot edit account settings (e.g., name, timezone, preferences, security settings) • Cannot edit device settings (e.g., camera name, timezone, location details, audio settings, operating hours schedule) • Cannot access device tunnels (direct device configuration interface)

editOperationalSettings.description:
Controls whether users can perform device operations or change technical configurations.
When false, includes all restrictions from editAdvancedSettings: false, plus additional restrictions such as: • Cannot control PTZ (pan, tilt, zoom during live viewing) • Cannot edit PTZ stations and presets • Cannot edit motion detection areas or other analytic configuration • Cannot share cameras with other accounts • Cannot turn cameras on or off

showBridgeHealth.description:
Controls whether bridge/CMVR health status indicators are visible to end users.
When false, hides health indicators such as warnings for CPU overload, high temperatures, high bandwidth usage, and video purge events (when video is deleted before it could be uploaded to the cloud).

enableVideoPrivacy.description:
Allows end-user account administrators to prevent resellers from viewing their camera feeds (both live and historic video).
When false, resellers have full visibility to all camera feeds and end users cannot restrict this access.

data.description: Structured audit details organized into sections for data-driven UI rendering. Each section represents a logical grouping of related settings or information, typically corresponding to a page or sub-section in the web application UI. The frontend can display new audit types and details without code changes by rendering these sections as labeled groups with rows of label-value pairs.

LabelValuePair.description: Represents a setting or piece of information displayed in the audit log UI. Each pair contains a human-readable label matching the UI, a machine-readable identifier matching the API field name, and the current value.

id.description: Machine-readable identifier in camelCase. Should match the corresponding API v3 field name when applicable to make it easy to relate the API and audit log.

label.description: Human-readable label displayed to users in the frontend application UI, matching the label shown in the corresponding settings screen. Should be written in English.

value.description: Current value of the setting as a string. Use empty string "" to represent "no value" rather than null.

type.description: Section type identifier. Currently only 'details' is supported. Additional section types may be added in the future.

id.description: Machine-readable identifier for this section in camelCase. Should match the corresponding API v3 field name when applicable.

header.description: Human-readable section label shown to users, representing a breadcrumb path to the corresponding screen in the web application. Use " - " as a separator for nested screens.

rows.description: List of setting changes or information displayed as rows in a table, each showing a label, current value, and optionally the previous value.

format.description:
Optional format hint for the frontend to properly parse and display the value.

pageToken.name: pageToken
pageToken.description:
Token string value that references a page for pagination. This value is received when retrieving the first page in the `nextPageToken` and `prevPageToken` fields.
When a pageToken is provided, the backend remembers search parameters from the original request, so search  parameters that affect the result set or order are optional and will be ignored if provided. Representation  parameters like `include` should still be applied.

pageSize.name: pageSize
pageSize.description: The number of entries to return per page. The maximum range of valid page sizes is documented with minimum and  maximum values, but the range might be further limited dynamically based on the requested information, account, and system status. Values outside of the (dynamic) allowed range will not result in an error, but will be clamped to the nearest limit. Thus, logic to detect the last page should not be based on comparing the requested size with the received size, but on the existence of a `nextPageToken` value.
